title: Fleet Capacity Ops — sprint handoff and day-of runbook
content:
Context:
This is the handoff note for Sprint 74 -> Sprint 75 focusing on capacity resilience, prewarming experiments, and the northbound routing throttles. Intent is to give oncall and next sprint engineers a compact, actionable view of current state, open risks, and who owns what for the next 72 hours.

Attendees (standup + handoff): Marcus Li (owner), Ana Patel (oncall lead), Ibrahim Khan (regional ops), Sofia Ramirez (platform infra), Claire Ng (SRE).

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Fleet utilisation: global GPU pool 81% current steady-state; burst-capable slack ~9% after safety buffer.
- Hot regions: us-west-2 at 96% during 10:00–15:00 PT window; eu-central-1 trending up, expected to hit 91% tomorrow morning.
- Prewarming experiment (node-priming v2): reduced cold-start tail p95 by ~220ms in small sample; needs broader rollout to 5% traffic for statistically significant metrics.
- Risk: preemptible node churn in apac-sg caused a 4-minute retry storm yesterday; mitigation in-flight.

Regional snapshots:
- us-west-2:
  - Utilization: 96% peak, allocated buffer has been exhausted for low-priority Dedicated bursts.
  - Recent action: bumped priority band for partner ingest routes between 11:00–13:00 PT; observed improved tail latency but increased retry rates for best-effort jobs.
  - Open tickets: INFRA-4217 (eviction spike triage) assigned to Ana, due 2026-10-22.

- eu-central-1:
  - Utilization: 87% steady, 91% projected next morning based on queued training jobs from internal tenants.
  - Notes: planned small-scale prewarm (50 nodes) at 02:00 UTC to soften morning ramp. Ibrahim to schedule and validate health probes.

- apac-sg:
  - Utilization: 73% but high variability due to spot preemptions in the cluster group 'g4-burst'.
  - Incident: 2026-10-20 16:12 UTC — transient node preemptions cascaded into 4m service retries for a set of canary routes. Root cause: region-wide spot reclaim.
  - Mitigation: temporary bump of fallback policy to use eu-central-1 for critical routes; Claire to update routing policy by 2026-10-21 09:00 UTC.

Capacity experiments and learnings:
- Node-priming v2 (prewarming small LRU cache on newly created instances):
  - Sample: rolled to 1% traffic in us-west-2 during peak window.
  - Result: cold-start p95 drop from 1.1s -> 0.88s (n=2000 requests).
  - Next step: expand to 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 48h A/B. Ana + Sofia to own metrics dashboard and rollback triggers.

- Autoscaler tuning (continuous-batch aware):
  - Observation: ramp-up latency remains the largest contributor to cost per token during short bursts. Suggested tuning: more aggressive initial replica allocation for routes with high burst probability.
  - Action: open PR (github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-ops/pull/512) contains conservative default adjustments; needs infra-leads signoff. Marcus to shepherd reviews.

Operational runbook highlights (what to do if you inherit this at 06:00 UTC):
1) Check global capacity dashboard (link in linked_artifacts) -> note any regions >94% alloc.
2) If any region >95% and p95 lat spikes > 2x baseline: immediately enable priority fallback for critical routes (ops-toggle), alert oncall.
3) For preemption storms: run 'spot-delta' script to surface recently reclaimed pools, then temporarily migrate canary traffic to fallback region for up to 1 hour.
4) If node-priming experiment fails (error budget > 2% for cold-start errors): rollback via k8s rollout pause and scale-down priming group.

Open action items:
- INFRA-4217: us-west eviction root cause triage — Ana — due 2026-10-22.
- Expand prewarming v2 to 5% traffic (us-west-2) — Ana & Sofia — start 2026-10-21 18:00 PT, monitor 48h.
- Update routing fallback policy for apac-sg transient protection — Claire — due 2026-10-21 09:00 UTC.
- Autoscaler PR review and canary flags — Marcus — merge window 2026-10-23.
- Cost delta analysis for priming (projected 2.1% infra cost increase vs. 6–8% latency improvement) — Ibrahim — deliver notes 2026-10-24.

Known risks & mitigation plan:
- Risk: Increasing prewarm pool size may raise cost baseline and artificially reduce pressure signals used by autoscaler.
  - Mitigation: gated rollout, 48h measurement window, rollback triggers tied to error budget and cost delta.
- Risk: Cross-region fallback increases inter-region egress costs and could surface rate-limiting in destination region.
  - Mitigation: limit fallback to critical routes, use token-based throttles, monitor egress budget.

Meeting artifacts and references:
- Ramp charts and p95 traces: confluence/redwood/fleet-prewarm-runbook-v2
- Related JIRAs: INFRA-4189 (autoscaler tuning), INFRA-4217 (us-west eviction spike)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-ops/pull/512 (autoscaler defaults tweak)

Notes to next shift (quick checklist):
- Validate that prewarm A/B flag is set to 5% and that experiment tag is present on traces.
- Confirm health probes for the 50-node eu-central prewarm group are green 30m after creation.
- Re-run 'cost-sim' script for projected 72h traffic; attach run id to INFRA-4189.

Appendix (raw numbers snapshot at 2026-10-21 07:10 UTC):
- Global GPUs total: 12,480
- Allocated: 10,106 (81.0%)
- Prewarm reserved: 330 nodes (2.6%)
- Burst slack remaining: 1,044 nodes (~8.4%)
- Regions over 90%: us-west-2, eu-central-1

Quick retrospective note: sprint handoff felt lighter when we codified the 3-step runbook two sprints ago. Keep the runbook simple and ownable; experiments are moving faster but need tighter cost gating.

If you pick this up — ping me on Slack @marcus.li or add yourself to INFRA-4217 watchers.
